events.notes: Read through the WebFetch summarizer (2.27 MB iXBRL document); two checks agree that 'Anthropic' is not named (document read; EDGAR full-text index has no 10-Q hit for 'Anthropic' in SpaceX's CIK). Blockspace/Business Insider reported $2.56B AI segment revenue on the earnings call (scout-2026q3) - a different basis than the 10-Q note's $2,194M 'AI Solutions & Infrastructure' line; not reconciled. Second read (verbatim) confirmed: Customer A 18.3% (Q2) / 17.9% (H1), all three segments; Customer B 19.5% (Q2) / 12.2% (H1), AI segment only; no other customer above 10%. Customer B's H1 share being far below its Q2 share implies its revenue began in or around Q2 (desk inference), consistent with but not proof of the May 2026 Anthropic agreement. Desk arithmetic: 19.5% x $7.814B = ~$1.52B for Customer B, close to the $1.6B of AI-infrastructure revenue from cloud agreements that SpaceX reported, and 18.3% = ~$1.43B for Customer A; Shotwell named Google and Anthropic as outside compute users on the call (Blockspace, T3), so B being Anthropic is plausible but remains inference. The 10-Q's $2,194M 'AI Solutions & Infrastructure' line and the $2.561B total AI segment revenue on the call are different cuts (not reconciled).

offering_structure.timing: DISPUTED sequence, not a clean split: late September (The Information, Aug 18) -> October (Quartz Aug 13; Business Insider Sep 13; PitchBook note of Sep 21 per the brief, not located) -> roadshow not before mid-October and listing days ahead of the November midterms (Reuters exclusive, Sep 4, via Forbes) -> November Nasdaq debut after Q3 results (WSJ, Sep 18; The Information/WSJ via The Decoder: 'late October at the earliest but more likely November') -> likely after the November U.S. midterm elections (Reuters and Fortune, Sep 29). No public S-1, price range or roadshow dates exist as of Sep 30.
offering_structure.share_classes: Class A common stock sold to the public (one vote per share); a single Class F share held by 'Founder LLC' (seven co-founders, directed by a majority vote of the co-founders) carrying 50.1% of total voting power on key corporate matters including some board elections; four other share classes (JPost copy); strategic-partner shares with very few votes (TNW); Amazon's convertible notes convert to nonvoting common on an IPO subject to an ownership cap (Amazon 10-Q); employees reportedly get their own stock to break ties on some issues (The Information).
offering_structure.lockup: Not in any opened prospectus coverage. The Information (Aug 27, Sep 3; relayed by BeInCrypto and Motley Fool): weighing lockups longer than the standard 180 days ('Insiders would take cash early, then wait longer for a second window') and preset 10b5-1 sale plans for rank-and-file employees instead of post-earnings windows.
offering_structure.secondary_component: The Information: early investors and staff may be allowed to sell shares in the IPO (a departure from the SpaceX playbook); not confirmed by Reuters/FT prospectus coverage. Nvidia reportedly weighing an anchor stake of up to $10B.
offering_structure.use_of_proceeds: Not reported in any opened source. Context only: the draft prospectus says demand for advanced AI is 'limited principally by the availability of compute', the company is shifting toward dedicated data centers and directly leased chips, and it has at least $518B of commitments (about 80% non-cancelable). Stated rationale (Daniela Amodei, Bloomberg Tech, Jun 4, via PYMNTS): 'It's a really big upfront cost to train the models and to serve inference on them' and 'the core set of companies that are working to advance the frontier are just going to need access to capital ... the public market is very well suited to that.'
offering_structure.ipo_debt_note: Pre-IPO revolving credit facility: more than $10B target (Bloomberg via Reuters, Aug 18) grew to $15B with 17 banks (Bloomberg, Sep 3). The brief's ~$10B matches the earlier target; no IPO-linked bond issue was found. The $34.5-35B TPU lease financing is SPV debt, not Anthropic-issued (scout-2026q2).
offering_structure.raise_disputed: Up to $100B at ~$2T (WSJ, Sep 18) vs at least $130B (The Information, Sep 3); SpaceX comparator $75B base vs $86.2B including over-allotment.
offering_structure.ltbt_post_ipo: Three trustees (Neil Buddy Shah chair, Richard Fontaine, Ben Bernanke) elect four of seven directors; Class F and Class A holders elect three (the two Amodeis plus one unnamed); Crypto Briefing says the LTBT gradually gains more authority over board composition. Founder special share phases out once two or fewer founders remain. Pre-IPO baseline (Anthropic T1 page): Class T stock lets the Trust elect and remove a number of directors, phasing in by time and funding milestones to a majority within 4 years, with one-year trustee terms and a stockholder-supermajority failsafe; whether Class T survives unchanged in the IPO is not reported.
offering_structure.status: Confidential draft S-1 submitted Jun 1, 2026 (Anthropic Rule 135 notice); no public S-1 on EDGAR at Sep 30; draft prospectus leaked to Reuters (and reportedly the FT) on Sep 28-29.
